title: Contemporary screen time modalities among children 9-10 years old and binge-eating disorder at one-year follow-up: A prospective cohort study
authors: Nagata JM, Iyer P, Chu J, Baker FC, Pettee Gabriel K, Garber AK, Murray SB, Bibbins-Domingo K, Ganson KT

primary_models.name: Multiple logistic regression of 1-year follow-up binge-eating disorder on baseline phone/SM hours per day, adjusted for sociodemographics, BMI percentile, site and baseline binge-eating disorder
primary_models.location_in_paper: Table 2, adjusted columns (aOR, p. 890); results text p. 890; interpreted in Abstract and Discussion pp. 890-891.
primary_models.design: Prospective longitudinal cohort with two waves. Screen time (exposure) measured at ABCD baseline (2016-2018, ages 9-10); binge-eating disorder (outcome) measured at one-year follow-up (2017-2019, ages 10-11). Single follow-up outcome, one observation per child. Baseline binge-eating disorder entered as a covariate. Each screen modality was entered in a separate model (each type of screen time modeled independently). No time-by-IV interaction (only two waves).
primary_models.sample: ABCD 3.0 release. Of 11,875 enrolled children, participants missing baseline screen time (N = 63) or one-year follow-up binge-eating disorder (N = 793) were excluded, leaving N = 11,025. Missing covariate data (N = 1,016) were imputed with Gaussian normal regression imputation. Baseline mean age 9.95 years (SD 0.63); 48.8% female, 51.2% male (including three intersex-male participants); 52.4% White, 20.1% Latino/Hispanic, 17.3% Black, 5.5% Asian, 3.2% Native American, 1.5% Other. Household income: 18.1% <$25,000, 20.7% $25,000-49,999, 18.0% $50,000-74,999, 15.7% $75,000-99,999, 20.1% $100,000-199,999, 6.7% >=$200,000. 79.7% with a parent with college education or more. BMI percentile mean 62.13 (SD 30.70). Table 1 values are propensity-weighted. Twins/siblings retained in the main analysis.
primary_models.iv: Baseline child-reported hours per day of each phone/SM modality from the ABCD Youth Screen Time Survey, one modality per model: texting, video chat (e.g., Skype, Facetime), and social networking (e.g., Facebook, Instagram, Twitter). Typical weekday and weekend hours were combined as ((weekday x 5) + (weekend x 2)) / 7 and treated as continuous hours/day. Baseline weighted M (SD): texting 0.24 (0.56); video chat 0.21 (0.52); social networking 0.13 (0.45) hours/day (Table 1).
primary_models.dv: Binge-eating disorder (binary, present vs. absent) at one-year follow-up per DSM-5 criteria, from the parent/caregiver-completed binge-eating disorder module of the computerized KSADS-5, with the KSADS-5 scoring system converting reported symptoms into a current diagnosis. Prevalence 1.1% at one-year follow-up (0.7% at baseline), propensity-weighted (Table 1).

covariates.name: Race/ethnicity
covariates.detail: White, Latino/Hispanic, Black, Asian, Native American, Other (parent report)

covariates.name: Sex
covariates.detail: Sex assigned at birth: female vs. male (male includes three intersex-male participants)

covariates.name: Household income
covariates.detail: Past-year household income, six categories (parent report)

covariates.name: Parent education
covariates.detail: Highest parent education, high school or less vs. college or more

covariates.name: BMI percentile
covariates.detail: From measured height and weight, converted to sex- and age-specific CDC percentiles; listed in Table 2 footnote and Abstract but not in the Statistical analysis paragraph

covariates.name: Site
covariates.detail: Study site (21 sites); entered as a covariate, form (fixed dummies vs. other) not stated

primary_models.equation: logit(P(BED_1yr[i] = 1)) = b0 + b1*phoneSM_hours[i] + b2..b6*race_ethnicity + b7*sex + b8..b12*household_income + b13*parent_college + b14*BMI_percentile + site terms + b_k*BED_baseline[i]; fit separately for each modality (texting, video chat, social networking). aOR = exp(b1) per additional hour/day.
primary_models.estimation: Stata 15.1. Multiple logistic regression with propensity weights based on the American Community Survey to yield nationally representative estimates. Missing covariates imputed via Gaussian normal regression imputation. alpha = .05; no multiple-comparison correction reported. Sensitivity analysis restricting to one sibling per family: 'findings did not differ', numbers not printed. Effect modification by sex tested for every exposure; all p > .05 except video games (p = .013), so no sex-stratified phone/SM estimates were reported. Age is listed among sociodemographic covariates in Section 2.2.3 but is not named in the adjustment sets in Section 2.3 or the Table 2 footnote.

Narrative only ('findings did not differ'); no numbers printed.

d_transformation.conversion_formula: d = ln(OR) * sqrt(3) / pi (Chinn 2000); applied to OR, OR_lo and OR_hi.
d_transformation.contrast_type: per 1 additional hour/day of the modality at baseline
d_transformation.notes: Chinn conversion of the aOR yields d for a 1 hour/day contrast, not a 1-SD contrast. Baseline SDs of the IVs are in Table 1 (p. 889): texting 0.56, video chat 0.52, social networking 0.45 h/day, so 1 hour/day is roughly 1.8-2.2 SD of these IVs; a per-SD rescaling would be ln(OR)*SD_IV before the Chinn step if needed for comparability. p0 = 0.011 is the weighted one-year follow-up BED prevalence in the full sample (Table 1), not an unexposed-group rate; it is not needed for the OR conversion. The outcome is rare (1.1%), so OR approximates RR.

extraction_flags: The adjustment set is reported inconsistently. The Table 2 footnote and the Abstract include BMI percentile, but the Statistical analysis paragraph (p. 889) leaves it out. Age is listed as a covariate in Section 2.2.3 but is not named in any adjustment set. I followed the Table 2 footnote. Site is entered as a covariate, but the paper does not say whether as fixed dummies or a random effect. Each modality was modeled separately, so each estimate is not adjusted for the other modalities. The aORs are per additional hour/day, while the IV SDs are only about 0.45-0.56 h/day, so the Chinn d corresponds to roughly a 2-SD contrast; reviewers should decide whether to rescale it to a per-SD contrast. p0 (0.011) is the weighted full-sample prevalence at follow-up (Table 1), not the rate in the unexposed group. Video chat (aOR 1.32, 0.99-1.76, p = .057) is recorded as non-significant.
